decisions.structure: CSharp shared enum and compiled frame-position getters supply the async factory/worker context prefix. SLG generated enum and function getters supply the corresponding factory/worker loops. Ownership analysis remains a consumer of canonical typed values, not the authority for these ABI positions.
decisions.branches: Five runtime pointers precede input/result/child handle/child context/spill/additional arguments; absent Unit input and scalar/aggregate payloads retain explicit size/alignment paths. Shared enum Count and generated layout admission precede field emission.
decisions.logic: Logical field roles and slot order come from shared CSharp declarations. Adapters use native CSharp struct GEPs versus SLG computed byte offsets and canonical type layouts; pointer transport does not invent a moved owner or transfer ownership of borrowed IO context.
decisions.diagnostics: CSharp contiguous enum validation and SLG fixed-layout admission reject malformed roles. Existing execution records are historical scoped evidence; this source registration performs no new task/cancellation/IO execution.
decisions.completionScope: Current named provider/consumer and phase ownership boundary only; no complete-file behavioral equivalence, new runtime execution, phase closure or defect-stabilization credit.

decisions.structure: CSharp constructor resolution and trait declaration registration commit canonical enum payload/receiver/associated types before ownership consumers. SLG resolved type references, selected generic-body specialization and declaration diagnostics provide the same upstream roles to typed ownership analysis.
decisions.branches: Option/Result parse in the active generic environment before nominal aliases. Trait declarations admit visibility, receiver and associated value types before unknown/missing/conflicting binding checks, independently of method presence.
decisions.logic: The source association preserves authority direction: ownership uses committed constructor/trait type facts. Neither helper is an independent ownership checker. SLG keeps source/owner identity in prepared type references and generic plans instead of copying CSharp bound-object representation.
decisions.diagnostics: Retain constructor child error priority and trait declaration rejection before LLVM. Prior types25240 evidence stays bounded to its original cases and epoch; no new generic-trait, whole ownership or runtime equivalence credit.
decisions.completionScope: Current named provider/consumer and phase ownership boundary only; no complete-file behavioral equivalence, new runtime execution, phase closure or defect-stabilization credit.

decisions.structure: FunctionSymbolIdentity is included by the frozen Shared source scope but its only CSharp consumers are backend Utilities.SymbolForFunction and CanonicalFunctionName. SLG frontend calls/type/ownership tables use declaration, module, AST and canonical type identities; backend appendFunctionSymbol supplies the separate LLVM reference envelope.
decisions.branches: Canonical qualification preserves already-qualified names; ASCII letters/digits/dots use the legacy encoding, other UTF8 bytes use uppercase hex. Local module suffixes preserve BMP letters/digits/underscore and replace each non-BMP UTF16 surrogate unit with underscore before invariant line/column suffixes.
decisions.logic: Do not introduce LLVM symbol spelling into semantic resolution, type identity or ownership decisions to satisfy source inventory. Current CSharp and SLG encoders are separate adapters, not an automatically generated shared algorithm. Existing source comparison documents their encoding responsibilities; whole future-change propagation is not established by this link.
decisions.diagnostics: CSharp has no semantic/type/ownership diagnostics in this value object. Native symbol-table admission and LLVM byte quoting stay at backend emission; no unqualified Unicode-async experiment or historical runtime result is promoted to current proof.
decisions.completionScope: Current named provider/consumer and phase ownership boundary only; no complete-file behavioral equivalence, new runtime execution, phase closure or defect-stabilization credit.
